**Finding submitted: deviation (LOL-CAP)**

- **What the document has:** Section 14.5 is the Agreement's only limitation of liability — a mutual waiver of special, consequential, incidental, punitive and indirect damages and lost profits, with the indemnities (14.1/14.2), confidentiality (Article XI) and IP (Article X) expressly preserved. Section 14.6 confirms insurance creates no liability limit, and no "aggregate liability" or other cap language exists anywhere else.
- **Why it deviates:** mutuality and carve-outs are fine, but there is no monetary cap at all, so both Parties' direct-damages exposure is unlimited. The fallback requires a mutual cap of at least twelve months' fees; as the paying party we bear real uncapped exposure on direct-damages claims.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** a single inserted sentence in 14.5 adding a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' payments and USD 1,000,000, with "Excluded Claims" (indemnification, confidentiality, IP infringement, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud) uncapped and Sanofi's payment obligations excluded from "damages".
